answer: Requiring every agent to lock a small refundable stake before trading makes fake identities expensive: a raven-like swarm of clones would each need its own deposit, so spinning up thousands costs real money. Like water slowly carving karst caves, honest agents build reputation over time that newcomers cannot fake overnight, and attackers who wander in with fresh wallets find no history to borrow. The stake is slashed on proven fraud, so Sybil farming loses money instead of earning it.
